AT.souhrn: Austria had 2,430 reported COVID-19 deaths per million by end 2022 (WHO data; 35th of 158 countries over 1 million people). A study suggests measures including a March 2020 lockdown curbed the first wave; the autumn 2020 second wave hit harder.

obdobi.text: Lockdown from 16 March 2020; R fell below 1 in early April and a study says falling cases suggest a strong effect of the measures. 455 deaths by 20 April, 432 aged 65+.
From mid-September infections rose to among the highest rates per capita; care homes did not stop admissions as in spring. The audit office found late decisions led to harsher, longer restrictions.

AT.vyhrada: A 2025 study finds excess mortality varied substantially across Austria's federal states and across pandemic years.

AU.souhrn: Australia had low COVID-19 mortality under relatively strict restrictions in 2020-21, eased once vaccination was high; deaths rose sharply in the 2022 Omicron waves, yet 2020-22 life expectancy trends were relatively favourable among high-income countries.

obdobi.text: Relatively strict restrictions went with low COVID-19 mortality: deaths were below expected in 2020 and only slightly above expected in 2021.
Restrictions eased once vaccination rates were high, and Omicron then spread; deaths ran over 10% above expected in 2022, mainly from COVID-19, and stayed elevated in early 2023.

BR.souhrn: A study ties Brazil's 2020 toll to uncoordinated responses amid deep inequality. In Oct 2021 the Senate COVID inquiry approved its report 7-4, recommending charges against Bolsonaro and others; its rapporteur said the government deliberately delayed vaccine purchases. Government allies disputed it.

obdobi.text: Analysing municipal data to October 2020, a Science study found that a lack of prompt, coordinated and equitable responses, amid stark inequalities, fuelled spread.
Gamma emerged in Manaus around November 2020, was estimated 1.7 to 2.4 times more transmissible and partly evaded prior immunity, then spread across Brazil from January 2021.
A study estimated that vaccination, which began in January 2021, averted about 303,000 adult COVID-19 deaths by the end of January 2022.

CN.souhrn: Zero-COVID suppressed transmission for almost three years. After its abrupt end, studies estimate about 1.4 million COVID-19 deaths in Dec 2022-Feb 2023 and 1.9 million excess deaths among people over 30 in Dec-Jan, far above official counts.

obdobi.text: Almost three years of zero-COVID suppressed transmission; mainland China's 2020-21 excess mortality was among the lowest compared with 74 other countries.
Rules were largely lifted on 7 December 2022 while vaccine coverage among the oldest was relatively low; a study links the abrupt exit without shielding high-risk groups to a surge in deaths.

CN.vyhrada: China reported nearly 82,000 COVID-19 deaths for mid-December 2022 to mid-February 2023, and WHO said its definition of a COVID-19 death was too narrow.

CZ.souhrn: Czechia had few COVID-19 deaths in spring 2020 but 3,946 reported deaths per million by end 2022 (WHO data; 10th of 158 countries over 1 million people). For autumn 2020, a review points to summer easing and weak tracing; the audit office also found tracing faltered as cases rose.

obdobi.text: State of emergency from 12 March 2020 and masks required from the start; 227 COVID-19 deaths by end of April. A review notes masks were thought to be a major factor in this early control.

According to a health policy review, most measures were eased by summer and the prime minister blocked a plan for indoor masks from 1 September. By early September cases were twice the 400 a day contact tracers could handle.
Alpha went from 0% to about 60% of sequenced samples from late December 2020 to late January 2021. A genomic study suggests it drove the winter wave; incidence peaked again in early March.

CZ.vyhrada: A 2021 review puts excess deaths in 2020 about 50% above registered COVID-19 deaths, so the full direct and indirect toll may be higher than reported.

DE.souhrn: Germany had 1,994 reported COVID-19 deaths per million by end 2022 (WHO data; 42nd of 158 countries over 1 million people). Its first wave saw comparatively few deaths; the winter 2020 to 2021 wave was much more severe, above all for older people.

obdobi.text: The response was generally praised for a robust health system, broad testing and contact tracing; many ICU beds, ventilators and doctors are cited as possible reasons for few deaths.
The second wave was substantially stronger than the first. Care home outbreaks rose about sixfold, with over 19,000 deaths among outbreak cases aged 65+.

DE.vyhrada: 2020 excess mortality was highest in the south of eastern Germany and lowest on the northern coast; in hard-hit districts it was driven by older ages and December deaths.

DK.souhrn: Denmark imposed strict measures by mid-March 2020 and had the lowest estimated excess mortality of four Nordic countries over 2020 to 2022, with wide uncertainty. Its reported early 2022 death peak was partly inflated by deaths with, not from, COVID-19.

obdobi.text: By mid-March 2020 Denmark closed borders and schools, going further than its health authority advised. First-wave mortality stayed far below Sweden's.
Restrictions were lifted in February 2022 as Omicron spread. Recorded COVID-19 deaths spiked, but an estimated 40% were coincidental, and the spike was not matched in all-cause excess mortality.

DK.vyhrada: Danish surveillance counted deaths within 30 days of a positive PCR test as COVID-19 deaths, so coincidental deaths rose when Omicron was widespread.

GB.souhrn: The public inquiry concluded that a lockdown about a week earlier, in March 2020, would have saved many thousands of lives. The winter 2020 to 2021 wave coincided with the Alpha variant, which studies linked to faster spread and a higher risk of death.

obdobi.text: Modelling cited by the inquiry put the cost of the one-week delay at about 23,000 deaths in England's first wave; the inquiry later accepted its summary stated this too definitively.
The winter wave coincided with Alpha, first detected in the UK in September 2020. A study of English community cases linked it to a 55% higher risk of death.

GB.vyhrada: By excess mortality the UK sat nearer the European middle: to mid-2022 its cumulative excess was 16th highest of 33 in an ONS comparison that also counted the UK's four nations.

HU.souhrn: Hungary had 4,958 reported COVID-19 deaths per million by end 2022 (WHO data; 3rd of 158 countries over 1 million people). A review of 2020 notes limited test sampling until late October and staff shortages.

obdobi.text: State of emergency from 11 March 2020 and hospitals told to free beds; 312 COVID-19 deaths by end of April. A review says the Visegrad countries effectively avoided the first wave.

A review of 2020 says test sampling was limited until late October, PCR prices were set low so some private labs stopped testing, and spare ventilators were sold for lack of staff. A study counts about 9,800 excess deaths.
About 8,100 excess deaths in this third wave. A study says lower relative mortality in older people was likely due to their rapid vaccination; relative mortality peaked at ages 35 to 44.

HU.vyhrada: Sources differ: a review puts 2020 excess deaths a third above registered COVID-19 deaths; a study finds excess over 18 months 1,700 below the official count.

IN.souhrn: A Science study estimated India's COVID-19 deaths by September 2021 at 6 to 7 times the official count, most of them in the April to July 2021 wave.

obdobi.text: After the first wave, restrictions were eased and testing declined. A parliamentary health committee later linked both to the scale of cases and deaths in the second wave.
In Delhi, Delta was estimated about 1.5 times more transmissible and partly able to evade prior immunity. The committee also cited mass gatherings and mismanaged oxygen supply.

IN.vyhrada: WHO estimated 4.74 million excess deaths in India in 2020 and 2021, far above reported deaths. India's government objected to the method.

IT.souhrn: Italy was hit early: the virus spread unnoticed across Lombardy before the first diagnosis, and demographers suggested its old population raised the death toll. A second wave in late 2020 caused about as many excess deaths as the first.

obdobi.text: Over 500 cases preceded Lombardy's first diagnosis on 20 February 2020. A model estimated Italy's restrictions cut transmission by about 45%, averting about 200,000 hospitalisations by 25 March.
The autumn wave caused about as many excess deaths as the first and spread more evenly across Italy, while containment shifted to regional colour-coded tiers instead of a national lockdown.

IT.vyhrada: In hard-hit parts of Lombardy in March 2020, official COVID-19 deaths matched about half of excess deaths; one study points to limited testing, though other causes may contribute.

JP.souhrn: Japan had fewer COVID-19 deaths per capita in 2020-2022 than most OECD countries despite one of the world's oldest populations, but excess deaths rose clearly in 2022 and stayed elevated in 2023.

obdobi.text: Deaths were below expected in 2020 and only about 2% above in 2021, a low toll for the country with the world's highest share of older people.
Excess mortality peaked at about 7.5% in 2022 and stayed near 6% in 2023.

KR.souhrn: South Korea had no significant excess deaths until late 2021; a study of early 2020 credits fast testing and firm action against community spread for early control. Its heaviest toll came in the early 2022 Omicron wave, hitting older people hardest.

obdobi.text: An early analysis credits rapid testing, firm steps against community spread and public awareness from the 2015 MERS outbreak for early control; excess deaths stayed non-significant.
Excess deaths rose from November 2021 and peaked in March-April 2022 under Omicron, hitting over-65s hardest; a model estimates vaccination averted about 112,000 COVID-19 deaths by October 2022.

KR.vyhrada: After the Delta period, excess deaths exceeded reported COVID-19 deaths in most age groups; one study suggests undiagnosed infections and disrupted care as reasons.

NO.souhrn: Norway's Corona Commission concluded the authorities handled the pandemic well, with one of Europe's lowest mortality rates, though preparedness was poor. Excess mortality peaked in 2022, after restrictions ended.

obdobi.text: Norway imposed a semi-lockdown on 12 March 2020 and traced contacts from the start. Its commission found vulnerable older people were largely protected from infection and death.
Excess mortality was highest in 2022, about 14% above expected, and roughly half was COVID-19. Deaths rose after reopening as testing fell; researchers say some COVID-19 deaths may have been missed.

NO.vyhrada: Nearly half of Norway's 2022 excess deaths had other recorded causes, mainly cardiovascular; researchers caution against firm conclusions from death certificates.

NZ.souhrn: New Zealand prevented widespread COVID-19 infection until almost everyone was vaccinated, and a study ranks its pandemic excess mortality among the lowest in the world.

obdobi.text: Border controls and Alert Level restrictions achieved elimination; with very little COVID-19 and fewer seasonal respiratory infections, deaths ran below expected levels.
When Delta reached Auckland in August 2021, a Royal Commission found no plan B for moving from elimination to suppression; long Auckland lockdowns followed and public support frayed.
COVID-19 spread widely only in 2022, after almost everyone was vaccinated; excess deaths then turned positive and closely tracked confirmed COVID-19 deaths.

PE.souhrn: Despite an early national lockdown, Peru had one of the world's highest COVID-19 death rates. Peruvian researchers point to a fragmented, overstretched health system, scarce ICU beds and oxygen, and weak health leadership.

obdobi.text: Peru had 5 ICU beds per 100,000 people, mostly in Lima, and little molecular testing. Researchers also cite health minister turnover and late cash aid amid hardship that drove people back to markets.
The second wave, in which Lambda and Gamma became predominant, was Peru's deadliest. Lambda, first reported in Lima in December 2020, spread rapidly in early 2021.

PE.vyhrada: In May 2021 Peru raised its official toll from 69,342 to 180,764 using broader criteria. A study found the reclassified count close to estimated excess deaths.

PL.souhrn: Poland had 3,120 reported COVID-19 deaths per million by end 2022 (WHO data; 20th of 158 countries over 1 million people); in 2020 excess deaths far exceeded reported ones. The audit office found the state unprepared, with no national epidemic plan.

obdobi.text: 624 COVID-19 deaths by end of April 2020. The audit office found converting 22 hospitals to COVID-only care significantly limited hospital access for other patients.
Testing largely targeted symptomatic people and tracing was limited. A study finds 37.5% of 2020 excess deaths were recorded as non-COVID, possibly unreported COVID-19 or poor access to care.
A genomic study notes the third wave, with deaths peaking in mid-April 2021, coincided with Alpha's spread: 87% of a Silesian cohort's samples in March, 97% in April.

PL.vyhrada: Excess deaths far exceeded reported COVID-19 deaths: more than double for March to December 2020 in one review; 64,037 vs 40,028 for 2020 in another study.

SE.souhrn: Sweden relied mainly on voluntary measures. It recorded far more COVID-19 deaths than its Nordic neighbours, but the national commission found its excess mortality through 2021 was under half the average of 41 countries.

obdobi.text: The Corona Commission found measures too few and too late in spring 2020 and said the strategy to protect older people failed; half of those who died by early December 2020 lived in care homes.
In the second wave the commission judged new measures reasonable but late, and said face masks on public transport should have been recommended earlier.
In 2022 Sweden's excess mortality was small and statistically uncertain, while Denmark, Finland and Norway had their largest excess after lifting restrictions.

SE.vyhrada: Other measures narrow the gap with Norway: one study found similar 2020 to 2022 excess mortality, another about 30% higher mortality in Sweden after bias adjustment.

SK.souhrn: Slovakia had the fewest deaths of the four Visegrad countries by end of April 2020 but 3,814 reported deaths per million by end 2022 (WHO data; 11th of 158 countries over 1 million people). Alpha worsened its winter 2020 to 2021 wave beyond expectations.

obdobi.text: Masks were required from the start and only 22 COVID-19 deaths were recorded by end of April 2020. A review notes masks were thought to be a major factor in this early control.

Bratislava hit tracing limits in August; a review says the prime minister overrode experts on weddings in October. Mass antigen testing plus restrictions cut prevalence in Oct to Nov; one study finds it temporary.
Alpha was about 75% of screened positive samples in February 2021 and 85% by 3 March. A study says it worsened the wave beyond experts' expectations.

SK.vyhrada: A 2021 review reports excess deaths from March to end 2020 more than double the registered COVID-19 deaths in Slovakia.

US.souhrn: US COVID-19 death rates were higher than those of most wealthy peer countries. Studies link differences between states to trust, poverty, education and access to care, and later deaths to lower vaccine uptake.

obdobi.text: From mid-May 2020, US death rates were higher than those of hard-hit peers such as Italy. A JAMA study cited weak public health infrastructure and an inconsistent response as possible factors.
Vaccination had just begun: by mid-January 2021 only about 4% of Americans had received a first dose.
In the Delta and Omicron waves the US had more COVID-19 deaths per capita than all 20 peer countries studied; the gap was much smaller in the 10 most vaccinated states.

VN.souhrn: Vietnam contained COVID-19 in 2020 with early, strict border control, tracing and quarantine; the 2021 Delta wave met a population with little immunity and brought over 32,000 reported deaths.

obdobi.text: A study links early, strict border control, contact tracing and quarantine to keeping spread in check; January to April 2021 saw 1,632 infections and no deaths.
Delta arrived when under 1% of people were vaccinated; with little prior immunity, non-drug measures no longer sufficed, and over 32,000 deaths were reported by December.

ZA.souhrn: Genomic surveillance in South Africa identified the Beta variant and, with Botswana, Omicron. Studies link higher hospital death rates in the Beta wave partly to strain on hospitals, while early Omicron infections were less often severe than Delta ones.

obdobi.text: Beta, first found in Nelson Mandela Bay, soon dominated in three provinces. Adjusted in-hospital death odds were 31% higher than in wave one, linked partly to hospital strain and possibly to Beta.
Omicron, detected in November 2021, spread fast in Gauteng. Early data showed it caused less severe illness than Delta, likely partly due to prior immunity.

ZA.vyhrada: SAMRC and UCT researchers found excess natural deaths to mid-2021 tracked official COVID-19 deaths but were about 2.5 to 3 times higher.
